runs_note: The exact run set this key was authored from; scoring must replay these and only these.
audit_note: The adversarial pass challenged this family's keys harder than any other's. A key flagged audit_challenged carries load-bearing defects its own auditor found; a score computed against it measures the key as much as the system.
session_notes:
Sixteen runs, all NEW generation (dip_snr / ambiguous / candidates / success_shape plus the min_dip_snr / dip_dominance / escalate_on_no_dip ladder); escalate_on_no_dip was False in every run, so both no-dip failures (#36, #84) were hand-escalated by the operator. Ideal total 8 runs against 16 actual; 8 wasted; 4 poisoned writes across two targets.

METHOD: every verdict here was re-derived from the runs' own ds_raw.h5 (I, Q, magnitude, phase, absolute frequency axis) rather than from the node's summary, so 'is this a resonance' was answered by the three-panel rule the family affords - amplitude notch depth relative to the LOCAL flank, unwrapped-phase step through the feature, IQ behaviour - not by prominence. Only two figure panels were opened, both on #39, the one decision that hinged on a picture.

THE RECURRING TRAP - PROMINENCE IS NOT DEPTH. On this chip a genuine notch drops R to 0.4-7% of its local flank and carries a 2-3 rad (~pi) phase step. The node ranks candidates by baseline-subtracted prominence over a structured background, and that ranking inverted against the physics three times: #39 (top candidate 4966.7 MHz at dip_snr 240.7 is the crest of an over-drive hump - R only 70% of flank, phase 0.17 rad - while the two real notches at 4953.7 and 4980.8 MHz ranked 4th and 2nd), #72 (5260.0 at 268 ranked above 5286.9, which is six times deeper), and #74 (5400.2 at 123 ranked above 5391.7, the deepest notch in the window). In every case the phase panel settles it instantly, which is exactly the cross-check this family has and the others do not.

A NODE-LEVEL DEFECT WORTH NAMING: on wide spans the emitted patch disagrees with the run's own reported fit by exactly 150.000000 MHz - #46 (span 500) fit 5116754663.94 / patched 4966754663.94, and #73 (span 300) fit 5259981417.42 / patched 5409981417.42, opposite signs. Both patched numbers land on smooth background. This is the wide-span LO re-centering path documented in max_escalation_span_in_mhz, and it means a wide sweep can poison the state even when its fit is describing a real (if wrong-owner) feature. Consequence for any reader: on a span above ~200 MHz, never trust the patch without checking it against the candidate list.

SPAN IS NOT A REMEDY ON A SHARED FEEDLINE. q1's 500 MHz sweep (#46) enumerates a comb of deep notches at 4738.0 / 4834.3 / 4954.0 / 4981.9 / 5085.5 / 5116.8 MHz - neighbour spacing down to ~28 MHz - and its top candidate is q2's resonator. q6's 150 and 300 MHz sweeps did the same. Widening after an ambiguous result reliably makes the ambiguity worse; the productive knobs after a failure were the readout DRIVE (#36: amplitude 0.0045 giving 6.4 sigma per point, notches present but only ~3 sigma) and the sweep CENTER (#71-#73 ran 100 MHz off because q6's stored readout frequency was 5301 rather than 5401 MHz).

WHAT THE FAMILY CANNOT DO. A 1-D magnitude sweep enumerates notches; it cannot assign one to a qubit. q1's window holds two equally deep, equally phase-confirmed notches (4954.0 and 4981.8 MHz) with the design prior sitting between them, and the node flagged ambiguous on all four clean runs. The assignment was settled outside the family - by 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power (#43 wrote q1 = 4982.3 MHz) and by 06_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_flux (#80 refined q6 to 5420.17 MHz; #91 found q12 at 5841.74 MHz after five 1-D runs had failed). The node's own docstring says as much under dip_dominance, and every ideal path here terminates by handing the residual question to 05/06 rather than by spending another sweep.

TWO FLAGS THAT MEAN OPPOSITE THINGS. success_shape=False with success=True is NOT a reason to reject a frequency - min_dip_snr is documented as the only gate on the frequency write - and q1's correct value came from runs that were all shape-failures (r2 0.76-0.81). ambiguous=True is the flag that matters, and it was raised honestly on every q1 run after the drive was fixed and on the correct q6 run (#79). Conversely, ambiguous=False was actively misleading three times: #38 (the competing notch was clipped by the window edge), #71 (a single edge-clipped feature 1.0 MHz from the low boundary, so nothing could compete) and #74 (dominance 2.02 against a threshold of 2.0, with three comparable resonators in view).

FINAL VALUES (with absolute numbers): q1 = 4981805126 Hz at #42, corroborated at 4982305126 Hz by the power node the same hour and at 4980836000 Hz in the lab state for the next three days; q2 = 5115271000.5 Hz at #51, single clean notch, one run is the whole correct session; q6 = 5420259154.8 Hz at #79, refined to 5420166103.8 Hz by the flux node one minute later; q12 unresolved - correctly, with the 5837000000 prior left in place.
adversarial_audit:
Verified every claim against `D:\work\Customer_Codes\CQT\data\2026-08-13` (node.json patches, per-run `quam_state`, `ds_raw.h5`, `ds_fit.h5`). The key is largely well-evidenced — dip depths, phase steps, both 150.000 MHz patch defects, #39's negative-slope fit curve, and the settled q1/q2/q6/q8/q9/q5 values all check out. But it has eight concrete defects:

**1. q1 #42 — false attribution.** "After the power node lowered the drive" is wrong: #40 **failed**, #41 succeeded, **both patched nothing**, and q1's amplitude is 0.1 at #39 *and* #42. The real 12 dB cut is readout-port `full_scale_power_dbm` 7 → **−5**, changed out of band. The key never reads FSP anywhere — same blind spot at #36→#38 (FSP 10→7 alongside amp 0.00447→0.1). Correction: attribute to an out-of-band FSP edit; step 2's prescription "amplitude → ~0.01, i.e. run 05" is refuted by the record — 05 ran twice and changed nothing.

**2. q6 caveat — contradicts the records.** "q6's flux offset was unchanged (0.25 V until #80)" is false both ways: `z.joint_offset` = **0.0** at #71–#77, **0.25** at #78–#79 (out of band; #78 failed, patched nothing). #74 and #79 are different flux points and not comparable. The "not settled" caveat and `confidence: med` should be replaced — a 0.25 V joint-offset step on a flux-tunable resonator is the recorded cause of 5399.9 vanishing and 5420.3 deepening 12×.

**3. q2 #57 — wrongly marked wasted; termination too early.** Not a repeat: #56 (06_flux, 19 s earlier) moved `joint_offset` 0.06108→0.05790 and `phi0_voltage` 3.6091→3.6457; centers differ (5114.766 vs 5114.965). #57 re-measures at a *new* bias, and its 5115210164.5 is the value the lab carried through 08-16 — as the key's own `value_evidence` says. Terminate at #57; `ideal_length` 2, `wasted_runs` empty.

**4. q6 #74 — q10 attribution unsafe.** "Lab settled q10 at 5392.745" reads `q10.resonator.f_01`, but the same record has `RF_frequency` 5422.745 (exactly +30.000000 MHz — q10 is the only qubit so split) and `frequency_bare` 5417.09. On that reading q10 sits ~2.5 MHz from the 5420.27 notch assigned to q6 — inside the linewidth. The 5391.7 owner is unidentified, and a q6/q10 ambiguity goes unmentioned while q6 is declared `unresolved:false`/high.

**5. q1 #47/#48.** "#47's only effect was to undo #46's damage" — #47 patched **nothing**; state still held 4966754663.94. **#48** wrote 4981940037.98 and repaired it. The one repairing run is graded wasted.

**6. q12 #85.** "None produced a usable value" — #85 returned 5953.859 MHz, dip_snr 22.53, r²=0.948, `success_shape=True`, `ambiguous=False`: a confident false positive at span 300, the key's own "span is not a remedy" trap, flattened to a null.

**7. q6 self-contradiction.** 5391.77 called "identical in #74 and #79 (0.42% / 2.3%)"; measured 0.32% vs 1.30% (~4× shallower). It cannot be the fixed reference licensing the "vanished" verdict.

**8. q1 ideal path is stitched.** Step 1 prescribes drive ~0.05; step 2 then grades #39, taken at 0.1 — the hump trap exists only because of the over-drive. Following step 1 plausibly gives a clean two-notch sweep, so `ideal_length` is 2, not 3. The key concedes this class for q6 but not q1.

Minor: "#46 … q2's measurement 12 hours later" — actually ~5 h 50 m (12:05:30 → 17:47/17:56).

ideal_path.expected_case: NEW generation (dip_snr/ambiguous/candidates/success_shape + escalation ladder; escalate_on_no_dip=False). success=False, dip_snr=0.0, candidates=[] - an HONEST no-dip, not a fit failure. Hindsight on the raw trace: q1's two real notches ARE inside the swept window 4916.00-5015.50 MHz, at ~4954.0 and ~4982.0 MHz (R falls to ~10% of its local flank at both). They are subthreshold for two compounding reasons: the readout drive is amplitude 0.00447, so the whole trace sits at ~6.4 sigma per point (median R 9.63e-5, per-point noise 1.51e-5), and frequency_step_in_mhz=0.5 puts only 2-3 points across a ~2 MHz-wide notch. Each dip therefore clears only ~3 sigma against min_dip_snr=6. A drive-level and sampling failure, NOT a span failure.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Do not narrow the span. Raise q1's readout drive (qubits.q1.resonator.operations.readout.amplitude 0.0045 -> ~0.05, i.e. run 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power first), set frequency_step_in_mhz=0.1 and num_shots=200, and KEEP frequency_span_in_mhz=100 on the 4966.0 MHz prior.
ideal_path.operator_did: Raised the readout amplitude 0.00447 -> 0.1, step 0.5 -> 0.1, shots 100 -> 200, but ALSO narrowed the span 100 -> 30 MHz (#38).

ideal_path.expected_case: Window 4916.0-5015.9 MHz, step 0.1, 200 shots, drive amplitude 0.1. Hindsight: exactly TWO real resonances, 4953.7 MHz (R -> 3.6% of local flank, ~2.94 rad phase step) and 4980.8 MHz (R -> 2.1%, ~2.55 rad) - both confirmed by the detrended-phase panel, which shows two sharp pi-sized discontinuities at detuning -12.3 and +14.8 MHz and NOTHING anywhere else. The node's top candidate, 4966.7 MHz at dip_snr=240.7, is the crest of a large background hump created by over-driving (R only 70% of flank, phase excursion 0.17 rad, no IQ closure) - the textbook Fano/structured-background trap: the tallest excursion in the panel is not the resonance. Worse, the reported f0 = 4960.300 MHz matches NO candidate in its own list and no feature in the data: the Lorentzian slid onto the smooth flank between the 4953.7 notch and the hump, and the plotted fit curve takes negative amplitude values while still scoring r2=0.963. success=True, success_shape=True and ambiguous=False are all wrong here.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Reject the fit and revert f_01/RF_frequency to 4966000000 Hz. Drop the readout drive roughly 10x (amplitude 0.1 -> ~0.01, i.e. run 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power) so the background hump collapses, then re-take the SAME window: frequency_span_in_mhz=100, frequency_step_in_mhz=0.1, num_shots=200.
ideal_path.operator_did: Accepted it and wrote 4960300000.0 to q1 f_01 and RF_frequency over the 4966000000 prior; then ran 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power (#40/#41), which did lower the drive.

ideal_path.expected_case: Same span/step after the power node lowered the drive (median R 1.62e-3 -> 3.02e-4). The hump is gone and the candidate list is finally the two REAL notches: 4981.8 MHz (dip_snr 25.75, R -> 2.8% of flank, ~2.96 rad phase step) and 4953.7 MHz (13.86, R -> 3.0%, ~4.34 rad). dominance 1.86 < dip_dominance=2.0 so ambiguous=True; r2=0.794 so success_shape=False - and by this node's own documented contract min_dip_snr is the ONLY gate on the frequency write while R2/FWHM/contrast guard success_shape alone, so the shape failure is not a reason to reject the frequency. The honest limit is that a 1-D magnitude sweep cannot say WHICH of two genuine notches on a shared feedline belongs to q1; the prominence ranking favours 4981.8 by ~1.9x and does so consistently at every later sweep center.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Adopt 4981805126 Hz as provisional, record ambiguous=True, and STOP the 03 chain. Confirm the assignment with 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power punch-out or 06_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_flux - not with more 1-D sweeps. Never raise frequency_span_in_mhz beyond ~100 MHz for this qubit: the feedline's neighbour spacing is ~28 MHz and a wider sweep only harvests other qubits' resonators.

termination.reason: By #42 the window's two real notches are enumerated at a drive level where neither is distorted, and the pick is as good as a 1-D magnitude sweep can make it. Every later 03 run reproduces 4981.9 +/- 0.05 MHz against a 5.4 MHz linewidth and adds nothing, while widening the span past ~100 MHz only harvests feedline neighbours (which is exactly what #46 did). The residual question - which of the two notches is q1's - is not answerable inside this family and must go to 05/06.
termination.value_evidence: A deep notch at 4981.7-4982.0 MHz appears in every clean sweep: #42 R -> 2.8% of local flank with a ~pi phase step, #45 4981.905, #47 4981.955, #48 4981.955, and #46's 500 MHz sweep 4981.939 with R -> 1.5%. It is stable in ABSOLUTE frequency across five different sweep centers (4960.3 / 4966.0 / 4966.7 / 4982.3 / 4981.9), which rules out an IF or LO artifact. Independently confirmed the same hour by 05_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power (#43), which wrote q1 f_01 = 4982305126 Hz, and the lab's own state carried q1 = 4980836000 Hz unchanged from 2026-08-14 through 2026-08-16.

wasted_runs.why_wasted: Narrowing to a 30 MHz span is the wrong direction after a no-dip failure, and the resulting window 4951.0-4980.9 MHz put its HIGH edge exactly on the second real notch (4980.8 MHz, the last-but-one point, R -> 0.8% of flank). With the competitor edge-clipped away the node reported ambiguous=False and picked the sub-dominant 4953.7 notch with a deceptively clean r2=0.987. Its information is a strict subset of #39, which ran 32 seconds later.

Re-measures the same two notches at a new center (4982.26 MHz); absolute stability had already been demonstrated by #39 and #42 at two different centers. Returned 4981.905/4954.005 - a 0.1 MHz refinement of a 5.3 MHz-wide notch.

500 MHz span on a shared readout feedline. It swept 4731.9-5231.8 MHz and its top candidate is q2's resonator at 5116.8 MHz (q2's own measurement 12 hours later: 5115.2 MHz); the deep-notch inventory of that sweep is 4738.0 / 4834.3 / 4954.0 / 4981.9 / 5085.5 / 5116.8 MHz - a comb of other qubits. It also produced a corrupted patch (see poisoned_writes).

poisoned_writes.why: Wrote 4960300000.0 over the 4966000000 prior. 4960.3 MHz is not in the run's own candidate list and is not a feature in the data - it is the smooth flank between the 4953.7 MHz notch and an over-drive background hump. The Lorentzian plotted with it takes negative R values. This value then became the sweep center for #42, and every later center in the q1 chain descends from a fit that matched nothing.

Wrote 4966754663.94 while the run's own reported fit was 5116754663.94 - exactly 150.000000 MHz apart. The fit itself had locked onto q2's resonator (~5116.8 MHz), and the patched number corresponds to no feature in any q1 sweep (the 4966-4967 MHz region is background in every clean trace). Node-level defect of the wide-span LO re-centering path; the same +/-150 MHz mismatch appears in q6's #73 with the opposite sign.

qubits.caveats: The 03 family alone can never assign a notch to a qubit on a multiplexed feedline - it can only enumerate notches. The 4954.0 and 4981.9 MHz notches are equally deep and equally phase-confirmed, and the design prior (4966.0 MHz) sits almost exactly between them (12.0 MHz above one, 15.8 MHz below the other), so proximity does not decide it either. Two further traps made this target adversarial: the neighbouring design value in this chip's table is q8 = 4981 MHz, which makes the correct pick look like a neighbour-grab (in fact q8 settled at 4991.2 MHz), and at the 0.1 drive amplitude used in #38/#39 the trace between the two notches is inflated into a hump 3x above the background, which is what captured both the peak finder and the Lorentzian. The confirmation that closes the case (05_vs_power #43 writing 4982.3 MHz, and three days of stable lab state at 4980.836 MHz) is hindsight from outside this family.

qubits.caveats: Two things about q6 are recorded rather than fully explained. First, the 5301 MHz sweep center that framed #71-#73 was set outside the node system (no patch in the day's record moves q6 from 5401 to 5301), so the answer key can state that the center was ~100 MHz wrong but not who made it so. Second, the physics of the 5399.9 MHz notch disappearing between #74 and #79 is not settled from this family alone: q6's flux offset was unchanged (0.25 V until #80), the two intervening flux nodes #77/#78 both FAILED, and the intervening power node patched q1's amplitude rather than q6's - so 'the resonator moved' and 'a spurious feature came and went' are both live readings. Either way the terminal value is the same, because the surviving deep notch at 5420.3 MHz is the one the flux node refined and the one the lab kept for the following three days. Marked med rather than high because whether #74 is genuinely needed on the ideal path - as opposed to going straight from #71 to a correctly re-centered #79-shaped sweep - depends on the runs that happen to exist.
